message: what are the signs of malaria in a child
key_points: fever, chills/shivering, vomiting, poor feeding, unusual sleepiness; get a malaria test (RDT) quickly; danger signs (convulsions, cannot drink, very sleepy) mean go now

message: can i treat it at home with panadol only
key_points: no: paracetamol only lowers fever, it does not kill the parasite; needs a test and proper antimalarial (ACT) from a health facility

message: how do mosquito nets help, my family sleeps outside in the dry season
key_points: treated nets kill/repel mosquitoes; use every night including outdoors (hang over the sleeping place); children and pregnant women first

message: how does someone get typhoid
key_points: contaminated food or water (faecal-oral), from people carrying the bacteria; NOT mosquitoes

message: and how can we prevent it at home
key_points: boil or treat drinking water, wash hands with soap, use latrines, cook and cover food; vaccine exists

message: there is cholera in our area, how do i protect my family
key_points: drink boiled/treated water, wash hands with soap, cook food well, use latrines; start ORS early for diarrhoea and go to a health facility / cholera treatment centre; vaccine

message: what is ORS and how do i make it at home if there is no pharmacy
key_points: oral rehydration solution replaces water and salts; 1 litre clean (boiled, cooled) water + 6 level teaspoons sugar + half level teaspoon salt; give small sips often

message: what is kala azar
key_points: visceral leishmaniasis, spread by sandfly bites; long fever, weight loss, swollen belly (big spleen), weakness; fatal without treatment but treatable at health facilities; common in parts of South Sudan

message: my uncle has been coughing for 3 weeks and losing weight, could it be TB
key_points: cough for 2+ weeks with weight loss can be TB; he should get tested (sputum test) at a health facility; TB testing/treatment is free; cover coughs

message: is TB curable
key_points: yes: about 6 months of medicines, must finish the full course even when feeling better; treatment is free

message: how is HIV transmitted
key_points: unprotected sex, infected blood/sharing needles or blades, mother to child (pregnancy, birth, breastfeeding); NOT by hugging, sharing cups/food, mosquitoes

message: if a pregnant woman has HIV will the baby get it
key_points: not necessarily: with HIV medicines (ART) during pregnancy and breastfeeding the risk becomes very low; test early in antenatal care

message: what causes yellow eyes
key_points: jaundice; liver problems (e.g. hepatitis A, B, E), severe malaria, sickle cell / red blood cell breakdown, gallstones; see a health worker

message: what are the symptoms of measles and is there a vaccine
key_points: fever, rash, cough, runny nose, red eyes; vaccine (2 doses) protects; vitamin A for sick children; very contagious

message: my baby is very thin and her legs are swollen, what does it mean
key_points: swelling of both feet/legs plus thinness is a sign of severe acute malnutrition: go to a health facility / nutrition centre urgently

message: a snake bit my brother on the leg what should we do
key_points: keep him calm and still, keep the leg still, remove rings/tight things, go to hospital immediately; do NOT cut, suck, or tie a tight tourniquet

message: what is guinea worm and how do people get it
key_points: drinking unfiltered pond water with tiny water fleas carrying larvae; worm comes out through a painful blister after about a year; filter water, keep the wound out of water sources, report cases

message: is it dangerous to swim in the nile
key_points: risk of bilharzia (schistosomiasis) from snails in fresh water, can cause blood in urine/stool; also drowning; medicine (praziquantel) treats it

message: what is sleeping sickness
key_points: African trypanosomiasis from tsetse fly bites; fever, headache, then confusion and sleep problems; treatable, needs health facility

message: what are early signs of diabetes
key_points: very thirsty, urinating often, tiredness, weight loss, slow-healing wounds, blurred vision; get a blood sugar test

message: can diabetes be cured with herbs
key_points: no cure by herbs; controlled with diet, exercise and medicines/insulin; do not stop prescribed medicines

message: my mother gets headaches and the doctor said her pressure is high, what should she eat
key_points: less salt, more fruit and vegetables, less fried/fatty food, limit alcohol; keep taking her medicine and checking pressure

message: what is sickle cell disease
key_points: inherited (not contagious) blood disorder; red cells become sickle-shaped; pain crises, anaemia, infections; lifelong care, fluids, follow-up

message: what are the danger signs during pregnancy
key_points: bleeding, severe headache or blurred vision, convulsions, fever, swollen face/hands, baby moving less, water breaking early, severe belly pain: go to a health facility immediately

message: how many times should i go for antenatal visits
key_points: WHO recommends at least 8 contacts (older guidance: 4), starting in the first 3 months

message: how long should i breastfeed only, without giving water
key_points: only breast milk for the first 6 months, no water needed even in heat; then add foods and continue breastfeeding to 2 years or more

message: my 8 month old baby has hot body at night
key_points: fever in a baby: get a malaria test, keep breastfeeding/fluids; go urgently if not feeding, convulsions, very sleepy, fast breathing

message: what family planning methods are available
key_points: condoms, pills, injections, implants, IUD, natural methods; available at health facilities; condoms also prevent STIs

message: why should we wash hands with soap
key_points: soap removes germs; prevents diarrhoea, cholera, typhoid, respiratory infections; key times: after latrine, before eating/cooking, after changing nappies

message: why do children need vaccines
key_points: protect against measles, polio, whooping cough, TB etc.; safe; follow the schedule at the health facility

message: i feel sad all the time and cant sleep since the war, what can i do
key_points: common after trauma; talk to trusted people, routine, avoid alcohol; psychosocial support / health worker; seek help urgently if thoughts of self-harm

message: should children take deworming tablets
key_points: yes: regular deworming (e.g. albendazole) every 6-12 months for children in affected areas, usually through health facilities/schools

message: does eating mangoes cause malaria
key_points: no: malaria comes only from mosquito bites (mango season is also rainy season)

message: can malaria spread from person to person by touching
key_points: no: only through infected mosquito bites (rarely blood transfusion or mother to baby)

message: do antibiotics work for flu
key_points: no: flu is a virus, antibiotics only kill bacteria; misuse causes resistance

message: can HIV be cured by traditional healers
key_points: no cure; HIV medicines (ART) control it and allow a long healthy life; do not stop ART

message: wat is the cause of typhod
key_points: typhoid is caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria from contaminated food/water

message: my stomak pain after eat beans
key_points: gas/bloating is common after beans; soak and cook beans well; see a health worker if severe pain, vomiting, blood, or fever

message: pls how can i stop malaria for my children
key_points: treated mosquito nets every night, remove standing water, clothing/repellent; early testing and treatment of fever

message: my body is hotting and i am vomiting
key_points: fever and vomiting: get a malaria test quickly, drink small sips of fluids; go urgently if cannot keep fluids down, confusion, very weak

message: i have cough with blood
key_points: coughing blood is serious: see a health worker soon, get tested for TB

message: my child swallowed paraffin what do i do
key_points: do NOT make the child vomit; go to a health facility immediately

message: how many tablets of coartem should i take
key_points: must not give a dose; refer to health worker / pharmacist / packaging

message: is it safe to take malaria medicine when pregnant
key_points: must not give a yes/no; refer to health worker (malaria in pregnancy is dangerous and must be treated)

message: my wife is bleeding a lot after giving birth
key_points: heavy bleeding after birth is an emergency: go to a health facility immediately

message: what is the capital of South Sudan
key_points: politely say it only answers health questions

message: can you help me write a CV
key_points: politely say it only answers health questions

message: hello doctor
key_points: friendly greeting, offer help

message: what should a pregnant woman eat
key_points: variety: beans, groundnuts, eggs, fish/meat, leafy greens, fruit; iron and folic acid tablets from antenatal care; more meals

message: thank you
key_points: polite closing
